transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support, my name is Greg. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Greg. I am calling because our broadband sync speed has plummeted by half. We usually get seventy-four megabits on Fibre 75, but ever since the violent thunderstorm struck our village on Sunday night, our speed has been locked at thirty-six megabits! It's choking our entire household connection!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear your speed has dropped in half after that thunderstorm, Lara, that's really frustrating. Let me look at your cabinet port profile. First can you confirm your full name and the installation address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Lara Croft-Davies, 45 Church Lane, Matlock, DE4 3QW.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What street cabinet number is your copper line connected to?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our line connects to Openreach Cabinet 14 at the top of Church Lane.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What does your router status page show for your downstream noise margin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The downstream SNR margin is showing twelve decibels, and the line sync is capped at thirty-six point two megabits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Cabinet lightning strikes are entirely Openreach external physical assets, so speed drops aren't S-Net's responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What do you mean it's not your responsibility? You sell me the broadband! Thirty-six megabits is completely throttling our household! We have two people working from home on video calls and everything is stuttering!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the signal-to-noise ratio margin on your VDSL line card.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router status page shows twelve decibels SNR margin.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Lara. A twelve decibel margin confirms the DLM profile clamped your line after the storm, and I understand how disruptive that speed loss is for your home working. Let me reset that profile right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I really hope you can unclamp it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we have the cabinet telemetry open, the loop attenuation is showing twenty-one decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is twenty-one decibels typical for our distance from Cabinet 14?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, twenty-one decibels corresponds to approximately three hundred and fifty meters of copper line length.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That matches our walking distance to the top of the road.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And there are zero errored seconds logged since the cabinet port resynchronized.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the lightning strike didn't fry the line card port.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And we recommend keeping your router plugged in continuously so the DLM does not interpret power-offs as line instability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We leave the router powered on twenty-four-seven.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any surge protection strips with phone line pass-through sockets?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, direct into the master socket with the S-Net cable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Surge strips can filter out VDSL high frequencies, so direct connection is best.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And Matlock is scheduled for Openreach full fibre deployment in late twenty twenty-five.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We'll definitely upgrade to full fibre once it reaches the village.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Full fibre uses dielectric glass cables that are completely immune to lightning electromagnetic pulses.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will be ideal during summer thunderstorms.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you want gigabit lightning-proof reliability, you should pay for full fibre instead of complaining about copper.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Full fibre isn't even available on Church Lane yet, Greg! That was a completely rude remark!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I said, copper lines pick up electromagnetic pulses from nearby lightning discharges.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you reset the DLM profile on Cabinet 14 now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check which cabinet you are on again. What was that street cabinet number in Matlock?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you, it's Cabinet 14!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for forty seconds while I dispatch an automated DLM profile reset to Cabinet 14 port 28.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Lara. The cabinet line card has reset the target noise margin from twelve decibels back down to standard six decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router DSL light is flashing amber right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait about sixty seconds for the VDSL handshake to complete.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The DSL light has gone solid green!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Refresh your router status page and check the new sync speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refreshing status page... Downstream sync rate has jumped to seventy-three point eight megabits with a six point one dB margin!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now run a speed test from a computer wired to the router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running speed test now... Download speed is seventy-one megabits! It worked! Full speed is completely restored!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the lightning-induced DLM banding has been cleared and your full line rate is back.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That solves the speed drop completely. Thank you for resetting the cabinet port.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your billing email on file, it's lara dot davies at peakdistrict dot org dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the line record, the installation address is 45 Church Lane, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 45 Church Lane.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your line that I can assist you with today, Lara?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Greg, the speed is back to seventy-odd megabits, that's all I needed. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Lara, and have a good day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
